primary_meaning: God's gentle blessing, favor, or spiritual refreshment/revival poured out quietly upon His people
primary_basis: Hosea 14:5 (I will be like the dew to Israel)
Psalm 133:3 (dew of Hermon as emblem of blessing/unity)
Micah 5:7 (remnant like dew from the Lord)
Zechariah 8:12 (heavens give dew as covenant blessing)

alternatives.meaning: The Word of God or true doctrine that gently nourishes
basis: Deuteronomy 32:2 (doctrine drops as rain, speech distills as dew)

alternatives.meaning: Resurrection life or awakening of the dead
basis: Isaiah 26:19 (your dead shall live... for your dew is like the dew of herbs)

alternatives.meaning: Sign of divine confirmation or miraculous provision (as with Gideon's fleece or manna context)
The Holy Spirit's quiet, life-giving influence
basis: Analogical extension from Hosea 14:5 and refreshment imagery

notes: Across patristic, medieval, Reformation, and modern evangelical/conservative commentaries the dominant cluster is blessing/refreshment/favor; secondary readings (Word, resurrection, Spirit) are well-attested but less universal as the primary symbol. No major tradition treats dew as inherently negative.
